title: Whether the style has changed; the single beat
summary: Zardis says the style has not changed; early bands played one beat, with four-four only in last choruses.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Do you think the music in New Orleans changed over the years? I mean, you've talked about how it's changed recently. Yeah, yeah. You know. Mm-hmm. But do you think the style itself has changed at all?

Well, I don't think so. You know what I mean? It's different bands, but it's different ways, you know what I mean? And it's a fool like, you take a rock and roll player, you put him with a Dixieland band, well, he just, you know what I mean? It's just something different altogether. Yeah.
Well, now, what about those early bands? Like, did you ever hear Manuel Perez? Yeah, yeah, sure.
They're great bands. What sort of style did they play? Well, mostly Dixiel's.
But I mean, classic, you know what I mean? Yeah. Classics. Did they play, did they have the same kind of beat? No, just like I told you.
They didn't start off with that kind of beat like we started off now like that. All bands, they had that single beat.
Really? Can you think, now let's think of a tune. Down by the Riverside, you know that tune? How would they, how would they play it?
Well that's a single, that's one beat.
Yeah, well now can you sort of hum it how they would have painted before?

Well it's about the same, the same thing to play it, yeah. Just about. But I mean the time, you see what I'm talking about? Now of course we play it like old time, that one beat. See when we go out with that drummer, he'll give you that four on that, that, them last two choruses, see? That's right. You can't pick up that number special and play four four on that, unless, the boy just want to jump it, but I mean it doesn't sound right, you know what I mean? It doesn't sound like you can jump it. But if you play it at a nice time, you know what I mean? That's it.
